{{Short description|Russian ceramics engineer known for his claims  of inventing the gravity shielding}}
'''Eugene Podkletnov''' ({{langx|ru|Евгений Подклетнов}}, Yevgeny Podkletnov) is a [[Rossiyane|Russian]] [[Ceramic engineering|ceramics engineer]] known for his claims made in the 1990s of designing and demonstrating [[gravity shielding]] devices consisting of rotating discs constructed from [[High-temperature superconductivity|ceramic superconducting]] materials.

==Background and education==
Podkletnov  graduated from the [[Mendeleev Russian University of Chemistry and Technology|University of Chemical Technology, Mendeleyev Institute]], in [[Moscow]]; he then spent 15 years at the Institute for High Temperatures in the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]]. He received a doctorate in materials science from [[Tampere University of Technology]] in [[Finland]]. After graduation he continued [[superconductor]] research at the university, in the [[Materials science|Materials Science]] department, until his expulsion in 1997. After which he moved back to Moscow where it is reported that he took an engineering job. Since leaving Tampere in 1997 Podkletnov has avoided public contact or appearances.<ref name=Platt1998 /> There is a report that he later returned to Tampere to work on superconductors at Tamglass Engineering Oy.<ref name="Painovoimaa" />

==Gravity shielding==
According to the account Podkletnov gave to ''[[Wired (magazine)|Wired]]'' reporter [[Charles Platt (author)|Charles Platt]] in a 1996 phone interview, during a 1992 experiment with a rotating superconducting disc:
 
:"Someone in the laboratory was smoking a pipe, and the pipe smoke rose in a column above the superconducting disc. So we placed a ball-shaped magnet above the disc, attached to a balance. The balance behaved strangely. We substituted a nonmagnetic material, silicon, and still the balance was very strange. We found that any object above the disc lost some of its weight, and we found that if we rotated the disc, the effect was increased."<ref name=Platt1998>{{cite news|last=Platt|first=Charles|title=Breaking the Law of Gravity|url=https://www.wired.com/1998/03/antigravity/|access-date=2011-06-19|newspaper=Wired|date=June 3, 1998}}</ref>

===Public controversy===
Podkletnov's first peer-reviewed paper on the apparent gravity-modification effect, published in 1992, attracted little notice.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Podkletnov|first1=E|last2=Nieminen|first2=R |title=A possibility of gravitational force shielding by bulk YBa2Cu3O7−x superconductor|journal=[[Physica C]] |volume=203|issue=3–4|date=December 10, 1992|pages=441–444|bibcode = 1992PhyC..203..441P |doi = 10.1016/0921-4534(92)90055-H | oclc =  4645428548 | issn= 0921-4534}}</ref> In 1996, he submitted a longer paper, in which he claimed to have observed a larger effect (2% weight reduction as opposed to 0.3% in the 1992 paper) to the ''[[Journal of Physics D]]''.<ref name="withdrawn" /><ref name="withdrawn2">{{cite arXiv|first=Evgeny|last=Podkletnov|eprint=cond-mat/9701074|title=Weak gravitation shielding properties of composite bulk Y Ba2Cu3O7−x superconductor below 70 K under e.m. field|date=September 16, 1997}} This is believed to be substantially the same paper accepted for publication in 1996 by Journal of Physics D which was later withdrawn by the author.</ref> According to Platt, a member of the editorial staff, Ian Sample, leaked the submitted paper to Robert Matthews, the science correspondent for the British newspaper, the ''[[Sunday Telegraph]]''.<ref name=Platt1998 />

On September 1, 1996, Matthews's story broke, leading with the startling statement: "Scientists in Finland are about to reveal details of the world's first anti-gravity device."<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/htmlContent.jhtml?html=/archive/1996/09/01/ngrav01.html |title='Anti-gravity' device gives science a lift |work=[[The Daily Telegraph]] |location=London |first=Graeme |last=Archer |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050314023910/http://www.telegraph.co.uk/htmlContent.jhtml?html=%2Farchive%2F1996%2F09%2F01%2Fngrav01.html |archive-date=March 14, 2005 }}</ref> In the ensuing uproar, the director of the laboratory where Podkletnov was working issued a defensive statement that Podkletnov was working entirely on his own. Vuorinen, listed as the paper's coauthor, disavowed prior knowledge of the paper and claimed that the name was used without consent. Podkletnov himself complained that he had never claimed to block gravity, only to have reduced its effect.<ref name=Platt1998 />

Podkletnov withdrew his second paper after it had been initially accepted.<ref name="withdrawn">{{cite web|url=http://bp0.blogger.com/_X2tcLFEJnwU/RavF9AEHkZI/AAAAAAAAAAM/ZQ7DaXG1P04/s1600-h/podkletnov.jpg |first1=E.E.|last1=Podkletnov |first2=P.T.|last2=Vuorinen|title=Gravitational shielding properties of composite bulk Y Ba2Cu3O7−x superconductor below 70 K under an electromagnetic field|date=May 13, 1996|publisher=Journal of Applied Physics D|access-date=April 29, 2014}}</ref><ref name="withdrawn2" /> The resulting uproar over the alleged claims in the withdrawn paper is reported to be the primary reason for his expulsion from his lab and the termination of his employment at the university.<ref name=Platt1998 /><ref name="Painovoimaa">{{cite web|url=http://www.ylioppilaslehti.fi/1998/04/24/painovoimaa-kumoamassa/ylioppilaslehti.fi/1998/04/24/painovoimaa-kumoamassa/ |title=Painovoimaa kumoamassa|author=Vuotta Sitten|date=April 24, 1998|language=fi|access-date=April 28, 2014}}</ref>

===Attempted verification===
In a 1997 telephone interview with Charles Platt, Podkletnov insisted that his gravity-shielding work was reproduced by researchers at universities in [[Toronto]] and [[Sheffield]], but none have come forward to acknowledge this. The Sheffield work is known to have only been intended as partial replication, aimed at observing any unusual effects which might be present, since the team involved lacked the necessary facilities to construct a large enough disc and the ability to duplicate the means by which the original disc was rotated. Podkletnov counters that the researchers in question have kept quiet "lest they be criticized by the mainstream [[scientific community]]".<ref name=Platt1998/> Podkletnov is reported to have visited the Sheffield team in 2000 and advised them on the conditions necessary to achieve his effect, conditions that they never achieved.<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://arc.aiaa.org/doi/10.2514/6.2001-3363 |doi=10.2514/6.2001-3363 |title=Gravity Modification by High Temperature Superconductors |author=C. Woods |author2=J. Helme |author3=S. Cooke |author4=C. Caldwell|website=American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics |series=Joint Propulsion Conferences |year=2001|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

In a BBC news item, it was alleged that researchers at [[Boeing]] were funding a project called GRASP (Gravity Research for Advanced Space Propulsion) which would attempt to construct a gravity shielding device based on rotating superconductors,<ref>{{cite news| url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/science/nature/2157975.stm | work=[[BBC News]] | title=Boeing tries to defy gravity | date=July 7, 2002 | access-date=May 2, 2010}}</ref> but a subsequent ''[[Popular Mechanics]]'' news item stated that Boeing had denied funding GRASP with company money, although Boeing acknowledged that it could not comment on "black projects".<ref>{{cite web| url=http://www.popularmechanics.com/science/research/1282281.html?page=3| title=Science Does The Impossible: February 2003 Cover Story| publisher=[[Popular Mechanics]]| year=2003| access-date=April 29, 2014| url-status=bot: unknown| archive-url=https://archive.today/20070930015205/http://www.popularmechanics.com/science/research/1282281.html?page=3| archive-date=September 30, 2007}}</ref> It is alleged that the GRASP proposal was presented to Boeing and Boeing chose not to fund it.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.thelivingmoon.com/41pegasus/02documents/Project_Grasp.html|title=Gravity Shielding Still Science Fiction, Boeing Says|date=July 31, 2002|work=Space.com|first=Jim|last=Banke|access-date=April 29, 2014}}</ref>

In July 2002, an article by [[Nick Cook (writer)|Nick Cook]] in ''[[Jane's Defence Weekly]]'' reported about [[Boeing]]'s internal project GRASP — Gravity Research for Advanced Space Propulsion to evaluate the validity of Podkletnov's claims. The briefing obtained by ''Jane's'' says "If gravity modification is real, it will alter the entire aerospace business." The briefing allegedly says that Boeing, as well as [[BAE Systems]] and [[Lockheed Martin]] tried to approach Podkletnov directly and that "Podkletnov is strongly anti-military and will only provide assistance if the research is carried out in the 'white world' of open development."<ref>{{cite web | author = Nick Cook | author-link = Nick Cook (writer) | url =http://www.janes.com/aerospace/civil/news/jdw/jdw020729_1_n.shtml | title = Anti-gravity propulsion comes 'out of the closet' | date = July 29, 2002 |website = [[Internet Archive]] | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20020802222642/http://www.janes.com/aerospace/civil/news/jdw/jdw020729_1_n.shtml | archive-date = August 2, 2002 | url-status = live}}</ref>
